root.label: Causes of WWI, 1871–1914
root.gloss: How German unification, imperial rivalry, the Dreadnought naval race, rival alliances, and the Sarajevo assassination caused war in 1914.

children.label: Part 1: Unification & Empire
children.gloss: Prussian victory over France, French revanche over Alsace-Lorraine, Kaiser Wilhelm II’s Weltpolitik, and the two Moroccan crises.

children.label: 1. Unification & Bismarck
children.gloss: Bismarck unified Germany through Blood and Iron, annexed Alsace-Lorraine in 1871, and used alliances to keep vengeful France isolated.

children.label: Sedan & Empire at Versailles
children.gloss: Bismarck’s Krupp steel artillery crushed France at Sedan and crowned Kaiser Wilhelm I at Versailles in January 1871.

children.label: Blood & Iron and Krupp Guns
children.gloss: 39 fragmented German states divided; Railways and breech-loading Krupp steel.

children.label: Sedan Victory & Versailles Crown
children.gloss: Captured Napoleon III, 80,000 troops; Wilhelm I crowned 18 January.

children.label: → Imposed Punitive Frankfurt Peace
children.gloss: Toppled French Second Empire regime; Made Germany Europe’s industrial titan.

children.label: Upended European Balance of Power
children.gloss: United northern and southern kingdoms; Created dominant Central European Reich.

children.label: Frankfurt & French Revanche
children.gloss: The May 1871 seizure of Alsace-Lorraine and five-billion-franc indemnity fuelled decades of French desire for revanche.

children.label: Seized Coal-Rich Alsace-Lorraine
children.gloss: 5 billion gold francs indemnity; German troops occupied French cities.

children.label: Black-Crepe Maps & Conscription
children.gloss: School maps draped black crepe; Conscripted French boys aged twenty.

children.label: → Haunted Berlin With Two-Front Fear
children.gloss: Permanent Franco-German border hatred; Pushed Bismarck to isolate France.

children.label: Forty Years of Continental Friction
children.gloss: Poisoned Western European diplomacy deeply; Trained millions for future war.

children.label: Bismarck’s Isolation Diplomacy
children.gloss: Haunted by war on two fronts against France and Russia, Bismarck signed the secret 1887 Reinsurance Treaty to keep peace.

children.label: Dread of War on Two Fronts
children.gloss: Feared France west, Russia east; Worked to deny France allies.

children.label: 1887 Secret Reinsurance Treaty
children.gloss: Promised mutual Russo-German neutrality; Safeguarded Germany’s eastern frontier.

children.label: → Unravelled After 1890 Dismissal
children.gloss: Young Kaiser sacked veteran Bismarck; Allowed Russian treaty to lapse.

children.label: Kept Fragile Peace Until 1890
children.gloss: Cautious diplomacy balanced rival empires; Prevented Franco-Russian military bloc.

children.label: 2. Weltpolitik & Morocco Crises
children.gloss: Scramble for Africa rules, Wilhelm II’s aggressive Weltpolitik, and German setbacks at Tangier, Algeciras, and Agadir.

children.label: Berlin Rules & Weltpolitik
children.gloss: After the 1884 Berlin Conference sped African partition, Wilhelm II dismissed Bismarck in 1890 to chase "a place in the sun".

children.label: 1884 Berlin Effective Occupation
children.gloss: Sought rubber, copper, palm oil; Triggered rush into African interior.

children.label: 1890 Dismissal & Weltpolitik
children.gloss: 29-year-old Wilhelm II sacked Bismarck; Demanded overseas place in sun.

children.label: → Challenged France in North Africa
children.gloss: Envied British and French empires; Required colonies and battle fleet.

children.label: Scrapped Cautious European Restraint
children.gloss: Replaced treaty balance with bluster; Alarmed London and Paris alike.

children.label: Tangier & Algeciras Setback
children.gloss: Wilhelm II landed at Tangier in 1905 to split the Anglo-French Entente, but isolated Germany at the 1906 Algeciras summit.

children.label: White Horse Ride Into Tangier
children.gloss: Landed unannounced in March 1905; Tested 1904 Anglo-French Entente Cordiale.

children.label: Outvoted 12–2 at Algeciras
children.gloss: Only Austria-Hungary backed Berlin’s vote; Britain backed French claims completely.

children.label: → Began Secret UK–French Staff Talks
children.gloss: Joint military planning in London; Cemented rather than split Entente.

children.label: Deepened Berlin’s Encirclement Fear
children.gloss: Diplomatic bullying backfired badly; Left Germany isolated in Europe.

children.label: Agadir Gunboat Crisis
children.gloss: Dispatching SMS Panther to Agadir in July 1911 triggered Lloyd George’s Mansion House warning and Anglo-French naval plans.

children.label: French Troops Marched Into Fez
children.gloss: Suppressed Moroccan unrest July 1911; Berlin sought colonial compensation.

children.label: SMS Panther & Mansion House
children.gloss: Gunboat anchored inside Agadir port; Lloyd George warned UK would fight.

children.label: Lloyd George warned UK would fight
children.gloss: Lloyd George warned UK would fight

children.label: → Coordinated Entente Naval Plans
children.gloss: Feared German Atlantic naval base; Humiliated Berlin forced to retreat.

children.label: Brought Europe Near War in 1911
children.gloss: Turned colonial rivalry military; Hardened British resolve against Germany.

children.label: Part 2: Dreadnoughts & Blocs
children.gloss: The Anglo-German naval arms race around HMS Dreadnought, rival European alliance blocs, and explosive Balkan wars.

children.label: 3. Naval Race & HMS Dreadnought
children.gloss: Britain’s Two-Power Standard clashed with Tirpitz’s Risk Theory, HMS Dreadnought, the 1909 naval panic, and failed 1912 talks.

children.label: Two-Power Law & Risk Theory
children.gloss: Island Britain protected food imports with the 1889 Two-Power Standard until Tirpitz’s 1898 Naval Laws threatened the North Sea.

children.label: 1889 British Two-Power Standard
children.gloss: Over 60% British food imported; Matched France and Russia combined.

children.label: Tirpitz’s 1898 Naval Risk Theory
children.gloss: Reichstag passed High Seas Laws; Built warships on North Sea.

children.label: → Pushed Fisher to Redesign Fleet
children.gloss: Aimed to scare Britain neutral; Convinced Admiralty Germany meant war.

children.label: Threatened Britain’s Island Survival
children.gloss: Naval defeat meant rapid starvation; Alienated British public and MPs.

children.label: Dreadnought & 1909 Naval Panic
children.gloss: HMS Dreadnought revolutionised battleships in 1906 but reset the naval lead, sparking Britain’s 1909 "We want eight!" panic.

children.label: 1906 All-Big-Gun HMS Dreadnought
children.gloss: Ten 12-inch guns, steam turbines; Unveiled by Sir John Fisher.

children.label: Reset Britain’s Pre-1906 Lead
children.gloss: Made all older battleships obsolete; Germany competed from near zero.

children.label: → 1909 Chant Built Eight Ships
children.gloss: Feared secret Baltic ship docks; Government funded eight dreadnoughts 1909.

children.label: Whipped Up Mass Anti-German Fear
children.gloss: Sensational press fuelled naval hysteria; Kept Royal Navy ahead expensively.

children.label: Failed 1912 Haldane Mission
children.gloss: Lord Haldane’s 1912 Berlin naval truce talks collapsed, prompting Britain to concentrate battleships in the North Sea.

children.label: Haldane’s 1912 Berlin Naval Offer
children.gloss: Offered African colonial territory swaps; Sought slower German ship building.

children.label: Kaiser Demanded Neutrality Pledge
children.gloss: Wilhelm and Tirpitz refused cuts; Britain rejected unconditional neutrality.

children.label: → Redeployed Fleet to North Sea
children.gloss: Pulled battleships from Mediterranean ports; Guarded home waters against strike.

children.label: Ended Last Chance for Detente
children.gloss: Confirmed permanent naval arms deadlock; Tied British security to France.

children.label: 4. Alliances & Balkan Powder Keg
children.gloss: Triple Alliance and Triple Entente divided Europe while Ottoman decline, Bosnia (1908), and the Balkan Wars primed conflict.

children.label: Triple Alliance vs Entente
children.gloss: Germany, Austria-Hungary, and Italy formed the Triple Alliance (1882), answered by the Franco-Russian and Triple Entente bloc (1907).

children.label: 1879 Dual & 1882 Triple Alliance
children.gloss: Germany backed Austria against Russia; Italy joined central military bloc.

children.label: 1894–1907 Triple Entente Formed
children.gloss: French loans built Russian railways; 1904 French, 1907 Russian deals.

children.label: → Divided Continent Into Armed Blocs
children.gloss: Broke decades of French isolation; Linked Eastern and Western disputes.

children.label: Deterrent Shield vs Escalation Trap
children.gloss: Aimed to deter rival attacks; Guaranteed local clash went continental.

children.label: 1908 Bosnian Annexation Crisis
children.gloss: As Ottoman rule crumbled, Austria annexed Bosnia in October 1908, humiliating Russia and infuriating Serbian nationalists.

children.label: Ottoman Decline & Pan-Slavism
children.gloss: Crumbling Turkish rule freed Balkans; Austria and Russia sought hegemony.

children.label: Austria Annexed Bosnia Oct 1908
children.gloss: Seized Slavic provinces without approval; Sparked intense Serbian nationalist fury.

children.label: → Humiliated Russia Vowed No Repeat
children.gloss: German ultimatum forced Russian retreat; Tsar swore never yield again.

children.label: Lit Fuse Under Balkan Powder Keg
children.gloss: Blocked Serbia’s South Slav dream; Ensured Russia backed Serbia 1914.

children.label: 1912–13 Balkan Wars Surge
children.gloss: Serbia’s rapid victories in the 1912–13 Balkan Wars doubled its size, convincing Vienna generals to crush Serbia pre-emptively.

children.label: Balkan League Expelled Ottomans
children.gloss: Fought two wars 1912–1913; Serbia won both conflicts rapidly.

children.label: Serbia Doubled Land & Army
children.gloss: Boosted Serbian prestige and troops; Inspired Slavs inside Austria-Hungary.

children.label: → Vienna Sought Pre-emptive War
children.gloss: Feared multi-ethnic empire breaking apart; Hawks awaited excuse to strike.

children.label: Made Sarajevo Crisis Fatal 1914
children.gloss: Turned Belgrade into existential threat; Set stage for July ultimatum.

children.label: Part 3: July Crisis & 1914 War
children.gloss: Princip’s shots in Sarajevo, Germany’s blank cheque, railway mobilisation schedules, the Schlieffen invasion of Belgium, and causal synthesis.

children.label: 5. Sarajevo & The July Crisis
children.gloss: Five weeks from Franz Ferdinand’s assassination on 28 June 1914 to Germany’s invasion of Belgium and British entry on 4 August.

children.label: Sarajevo & The Blank Cheque
children.gloss: Black Hand conspirator Gavrilo Princip assassinated Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo before Berlin handed Vienna an unconditional blank cheque.

children.label: Princip Shot Archduke 28 June
children.gloss: Survived Appel Quay grenade attack; Wrong turn met Princip’s pistol.

children.label: Kaiser’s 5 July Blank Cheque
children.gloss: Promised Franz Joseph unconditional backing; Removed fear of Russian intervention.

children.label: → Emboldened Vienna’s Harsh Ultimatum
children.gloss: Austria resolved to crush Serbia; Ignored wider European war risks.

children.label: Turned Balkan Murder Into Crisis
children.gloss: Berlin’s guarantee freed Austrian hawks; Escalated local shooting into war.

children.label: Ultimatum & Rail Timetables
children.gloss: Austria shelled Serbia after its ten-point ultimatum, triggering Russian mobilisation and unstoppable European railway schedules.

children.label: 23 July Ten-Point Ultimatum
children.gloss: Demanded Austrian police inside Belgrade; Serbia accepted nine of ten.

children.label: 28 July Shelling & Tsar Mobilised
children.gloss: Danube gunboats shelled Belgrade 28th; Tsar Nicholas called up millions.

children.label: → Activated Rigid Railway Timetables
children.gloss: Trains carried millions toward borders; Halting schedules risked total defeat.

children.label: Military Clocks Overtook Diplomacy
children.gloss: Generals feared being caught unready; Triggered automatic alliance chain reaction.

children.label: Schlieffen Plan & Belgium
children.gloss: Executing the Schlieffen Plan, German troops invaded neutral Belgium on 4 August 1914, bringing Great Britain into the world war.

children.label: Schlieffen Two-Front Knockout Plan
children.gloss: Aimed to defeat France fast; Avoided slow Russian eastern steamroller.

children.label: 4 Aug Invasion & Scrap of Paper
children.gloss: German army marched into Belgium; Broke 1839 Treaty of London.

children.label: → Britain Declared War Midnight 4 Aug
children.gloss: Berlin ignored British withdrawal demand; Committed British Empire to war.

children.label: Completed Five-Week Descent to War
children.gloss: Turned continental clash global; Ended century of general peace.

children.label: 6. Synthesis: Outbreak of War
children.gloss: Connecting long-term unification, imperial rivalry, dreadnoughts, and alliances to the July 1914 Sarajevo trigger.

children.label: Unification & Imperial Rivalry
children.gloss: 1871 German unification and Weltpolitik clashes in Africa and Morocco permanently alienated France and Great Britain.

children.label: 1871 Alsace-Lorraine Divided Powers
children.gloss: Unified 39 states after 1870; Fuelled 40 years French revanchism.

children.label: Weltpolitik & Moroccan Bullying
children.gloss: Competed for African rubber, copper; Morocco crises united Britain, France.

children.label: → Hardened Hostile Great-Power Rivalry
children.gloss: Ended Bismarck’s diplomatic restraint; Left Berlin diplomatically isolated.

children.label: Built Deep Long-Term Resentment
children.gloss: Split Europe’s strongest land powers; Made compromise harder in crises.

children.label: Dreadnoughts & Alliance Blocs
children.gloss: North Sea dreadnought competition and rival Triple Alliance / Triple Entente blocs wired Europe for continental war.

children.label: Post-1906 Dreadnought Arms Race
children.gloss: Challenged Britain’s Two-Power Standard; Tirpitz’s North Sea fleet panicked UK.

children.label: Tirpitz’s North Sea fleet panicked UK
children.gloss: Tirpitz’s North Sea fleet panicked UK

children.label: Two Armed European Power Camps
children.gloss: Germany, Austria, Italy Triple Alliance; Britain, France, Russia Triple Entente.

children.label: → Primed Continent for Chain Reaction
children.gloss: Bound great powers by treaty; Prevented localising Balkan disputes.

children.label: Turned Rivalry Into Hair-Trigger
children.gloss: Public demanded extra battleships; Staff plans assumed rapid war.

children.label: 1914 Trigger & Multi-Cause Verdict
children.gloss: Princip’s assassination lit the structural powder keg, requiring multi-factor PEEL links between long-term tensions and 1914 triggers.

children.label: Sarajevo Sparked Five-Week Dominoes
children.gloss: Princip killed Archduke 28 June; Austrian retaliation triggered rival blocs.

children.label: → Dragged Five Great Powers In
children.gloss: Activated Russian, French, German plans; Belgian invasion brought Britain in.

children.label: Long-Term Powder vs 1914 Spark
children.gloss: Alliances and arms stacked powder; July decisions lit fatal fuse.

children.label: Three-Factor Causal Essay Structure
children.gloss: Connects structural causes to trigger; Explains why localised war failed.
